Normal, generally positive recommendations plus excellent academic qualifications will be sufficient for admissions at many excellent US colleges. However, the most selective holistic review US colleges get so many highly qualified applicants they can generally afford to look both for top academic qualifications AND also what they deem to be very compelling non-academic traits. And studies have suggested recommendations can play a significant role in who gets very strong non-academic ratings at the most selective holistic review colleges.

First of all, if they are new teachers, they probably didn't go to college all that long ago so maybe they are very familiar with what should go into a LOR. Secondly, make appointments to talk to them after class, bring in interesting info related to the course subject if possible, and ask if you can provide them with a summary about yourself (including things you remember about their class and interactions you had with them in class that stand out in your mind, to remind them). Don't assume a letter will be mediocre. Pick teachers, even if new, who stand out to you and who think you are a student in their class who has made a difference.
